question: Can MTS manage destructive declines with two distinct causal pathways: (a) immediate full exit for a COVID-like fast shock signature, and (b) rapid full exit for slower recognized bear-market collapses followed by causal bottom-approximation reentry?
split_method: Rank the already-consumed 67 tickers by SHA256('mts-crash-50-17-20261004|'+ticker); first 50 development, remaining 17 untouched test.

fast_shock_design.intent: Describe causal contemporaneous conditions that occur in unison during the COVID-style fast shock; if matched, liquidate all positions immediately.

stage1_fast_signature: On development50 only, search sparse conjunctions of predeclared rolling stress-percentile features for the earliest COVID-shock recognition with low pre-episode false-alert burden. Trigger means selected stress conditions occur together. No portfolio-return optimization.
stage2_slow_bear_exit: On development50 only, search sparse rolling stress-percentile conjunctions for the earliest causal recognition shared across 2008, 2015, and 2022. Once recognized, liquidate all active positions at next tradable opportunity and block new entries.
stage3_reentry: After any exit, estimate bottom using episode-relative reversal geometry rather than fixed absolute levels: short-horizon return reversal, breadth rebound, negative-participation retreat, volatility contraction, drawdown improvement. Reopen MTS on the next tradable session after confirmation.
test17: After architecture and parameters are frozen on development50, construct the same causal state from test17 and run exactly once with no repair.
success: Test17 should materially reduce destructive-period drawdowns while retaining substantially more wealth/CAGR than prior always-on risk overlays. Report failure as failure.
